newsitem.title: JAPAN: Shorter JGB settlement increasing dealers' costs.
newsitem.headline: Shorter JGB settlement increasing dealers' costs.

text.p: The introduction of a "T plus three" (T+3) rolling settlement has not led to major confusion in the Japanese government bond (JGB) market, but securities companies now face greater costs in their efforts to avoid settlement problems, bond traders said on Tuesday.
Starting from April 21, the settlement period for JGB transactions was shortened by four business days.

Under the old "T plus seven" (T+7) rolling settlement introduced last autumn, JGB settlement took place seven business days after a trade. From Monday, this has been been shortened to three business days.
"We have not heard of any notable problems occurring after the introduction of T+3. That is probably because securities companies were well-prepared," said a manager at a second-tier brokerage house.
However, T+3 is putting the securities companies under greater cost burdens, traders said.

"So far, we have not seen any great impact from T+3 on daily JGB trading. But risks of settlement-related troubles have definitely increased with the shortening of the settlement period," said a manager at a city bank's securities unit.
"Under the T+3 system, dealers will have less time to find solutions when problems occur," he added.
With the start of T+3, bond dealers now prefer longer-dated transactions when they borrow bonds in the repo market, traders said.
This is because dealers now have fewer days to procure cash bonds when their counterparties fail to deliver bonds on time, they said.

"Even when dealers actually need to borrow bonds for only a day or two, they are choosing to borrow for one or two weeks to make sure they have cash bonds in hand. This has resulted in greater cost burdens for securities companies," said the manager for the city bank's securities unit.
The rolling settlement system for JGB transactions was introduced in September 1996.
Before that, JGB settlements took place on fixed dates -- the 5th, 10th, 15th, 20th, 25th and 30th of each month -- and settling JGB transactions took seven to 11 business days.

Analysts said the introduction of a rolling settlement was a step in the right direction for Japan's goal to move its financial markets closer to global standards. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
